extracted.intended_audience: Founders, engineers, makers, and marketers who want to post or market content on Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for submitting links, Ask HN posts, and Show HN projects to Hacker News so they avoid being treated as spam and maximize the chance of useful discussion or visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit the original source
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the original source when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you can, link to the original material rather than a repost or summary. This increases credibility and avoids removals or user criticism for not citing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a neutral/plain title
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a neutral title. Do not add hype, site names, exclamation points, or marketing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN titles should be clear, neutral, and close to the original title. Avoid uppercase, exclamation points, praise, gratuitous numbers, or editorialization (e.g., bad: '10 Amazing Lessons...' vs better: 'Lessons from launching our database migration tool'). Misleading or promotional titles may be changed by moderators or downweighted by users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the correct post type
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the format that matches what you actually have (regular link submission, Ask HN, or Show HN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most mistakes start here. Use regular link submissions for content where the link is the main thing (blog posts, technical writeups, research). Use Ask HN when you genuinely want answers or recommendations. Use Show HN only for things people can try and that you personally made. Choosing the wrong type makes a post look like promotion or a category error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular link submission: appropriate uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a regular link submission for blog posts, technical writeups, research, essays, news, tools with detailed launch pages, or anything where the link itself is the main thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is usually the right choice for content marketing. Ensure the linked page stands on its own for a skeptical technical reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask HN: when to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Ask HN when you want answers from the community; a good Ask HN is specific and useful to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using Ask HN as a disguised launch. A bad Ask HN appears to be a marketing post pretending to be a question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show HN: when to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Show HN when you made something and people can try it. Blog posts, newsletters, lists, sign-up pages, and landing pages are not Show HNs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show HN works best for dev tools, apps, hardware, open source projects, experiments, and small demos that are non-trivial, personally made, and ready for feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show HN checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist to confirm a submission is suitable for Show HN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title starts with 'Show HN:'. You personally worked on the thing. Other people can try it, run it, inspect it, or give meaningful feedback. It is not just a blog post, newsletter, reading list, landing page, fundraiser, or waitlist. It is easy to try without a signup or email gate if possible. You can be around in the thread to answer questions. You are not asking friends to upvote or comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles are shared labels; avoid misleading/linkbait titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Hacker News titles are treated as shared labels for discussion, not as ad copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the title is misleading, linkbait, or too promotional, users or moderators may change it. Treat titles as factual descriptors to help the community engage correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page fit: what tends to reach the front page
rubrics_metrics.description: A front-page post usually gives the community something to think about, test, correct, or argue with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful blog posts, technical writeups, founder stories, research, and small tools often fit better than product announcements. Successful posts invite informed disagreement or scrutiny rather than acting as pure promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe angles for company content
rubrics_metrics.description: For company-related posts, favor angles that provide independent interest beyond marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good safe angles include: a technical lesson learned while building something; a surprising failure, tradeoff, benchmark, or teardown; a firsthand founder story with numbers and consequences; a tool, demo, or dataset that readers can inspect; or a clear argument that invites informed disagreement. 'We launched a product' is a weak angle on HN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking factors and moderation filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Story ranking is affected by votes and time, but also by user flags, anti-abuse software, account or site weighting, and moderator action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two similar posts can behave differently due to flags, software downweighting, domain/account weighting, or moderators changing titles/killing posts. There is a second-chance pool where overlooked links may be reexamined. Write for readers and moderators, not only for an algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no magic hour, but timing helps at the margin: post when the US technical audience is awake and you can spend the next few hours replying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical default is 9am-12pm Eastern Time on a weekday morning. Treat timing as availability planning, not a guaranteed ranking trick. Do not post right before a meeting, flight, or sleep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare the landing page for skeptical technical readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, make sure the page can survive a skeptical technical reader arriving cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load fast; remove popups, newsletter gates, chat widgets, and aggressive signup walls. Put the demo, screenshots, code, result, or core argument near the top. Explain technical details and tradeoffs; state limitations honestly. Make pricing, availability, source code, or access rules clear when they matter. Have analytics ready, but judge success by feedback, links, signups, and follow-up conversations, not only points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use HN primarily for promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use Hacker News primarily for promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN users and moderators punish obvious promotional behavior. Repeatedly launching or treating HN as a marketing channel can lead to flags, downweighting, or kills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not solicit upvotes or coordinate voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask friends, followers, users, or teammates to upvote or comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hacker News explicitly forbids soliciting upvotes/comments/submissions. Coordinated pushes can trigger anti-abuse systems and poison discussion. This applies to private asks to employees or public calls for votes alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common behaviors that get posts killed
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid actions likely to get a post killed by software, user flags, or moderators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't delete and repost because the first try failed. Don't submit a duplicate if the story already got significant attention recently. Don't disguise a landing page as Show HN. Don't paste AI-generated or AI-edited comments. Follow official HN guidelines and FAQ to reduce risk of moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: First comment when submitting your own work
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit your own work, add one calm comment after posting to help start the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful first comment covers: who you are and why you made the thing; the specific problem, constraint, or weird observation behind it; what is new, incomplete, or technically interesting; and what kind of feedback would actually help. Avoid asking people to support you, explaining market size, or turning the comment into a sales pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing strategy via comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can be an effective marketing channel if you add real value to conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor relevant threads, reply early with useful context or caveats, and share concrete examples. Disclose your connection when you mention your own product. Skip threads where the only thing you can add is a link. Repeatedly forcing promotional links will be penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply authentically in threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply to comments like a human. Do not paste generated or AI-edited replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN readers are sensitive to inauthentic replies. Human, specific, and technically detailed replies are valued; pasted or obviously AI-produced responses can be flagged or damage credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text submissions cannot include links
rubrics_metrics.description: Text (self) submissions on Hacker News cannot include links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want discussion about a link, submit the link itself and then add context in a regular comment rather than using a text submission with embedded links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting moderators
rubrics_metrics.description: Email moderators only for moderation mistakes or account/title/posting problems; do not email moderators to promote your post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators can change titles, kill posts, turn flags off, move submissions, and downweight stories. Use hn@ycombinator.com for legitimate moderation issues (wrongly killed posts, unfair flags, title edits you think are incorrect). Do not treat moderator contact as a promotional channel.
